classification.zh: 加拿大七人画派的风景绘画：后印象派式色彩概括、装饰性轮廓与有节奏的地形
classification.en: Landscape painting of Canada’s Group of Seven: Post-Impressionist-like simplification of color, decorative contours and rhythmic terrain

summary.zh: 山丘像波浪般层层展开，云带与坡面相互呼应；明亮的橙红、金黄与冷蓝远景形成强烈对照。秋林中的白桦和深色针叶树构成竖向骨架，短笔触把叶丛、岩石和光斑织成有秩序的色块。本条以三幅可对应作品的用户复现图归纳风格。
summary.en: Hills unfold in successive waves, with cloud bands echoing the slopes; bright orange-red and golden yellow contrast strongly with cool blue distance. Birches and dark conifers form a vertical framework in the autumn woods, while short brushstrokes weave foliage, rocks and patches of light into ordered color masses. This entry summarizes the style from three user-provided reproductions that can be matched to identified artworks.

recognition.zh: 先看地形与云层的方向节奏，再看暖色亮部、冷色阴影和简化树形之间的关系。它与已有装饰插画的植物题材有交集，但更依靠风景的地形、光照与色块建立结构；既保留空间纵深，也有鲜明的平面设计感。
recognition.en: First look at the directional rhythms of the land and clouds, then at the relationships among warm highlights, cool shadows and simplified tree forms. Plant subjects overlap with those in the atlas’s decorative illustration examples, but here terrain, light and color masses do more of the structural work. Spatial depth coexists with a strong sense of flat graphic design.

reuse_focus.zh: 先按原照片重建大色块与明暗，再让笔触顺着已有形体走。开阔场景可侧重山势与云带的节奏；树林可侧重浅色树干、深色树群与暖色碎笔触。把参考色盘用于既有对象，保留原场景的结构和人物身份。
reuse_focus.en: Reconstruct the large color masses and light–dark structure from the original photograph first, then let the brushwork follow its existing forms. In open scenes, emphasize the rhythms of hills and cloud bands; in woodland, emphasize pale trunks, dark tree masses and warm broken brushwork. Apply the reference palette to existing objects while preserving the original scene’s structure and people’s identities.

judgment_note.zh: 作品信息与风格判断分开记录：年代、媒介和馆藏据各图下方所链来源；“后印象派式”“装饰性”是本图鉴对可见语言的概括。《Autumn》（1940）信息据 DailyArt 的 McMichael 专题，本次未取得馆藏数据库登记号；用户附图是裁去下部前景的局部。《Festive Autumn》采用 AGO 现行馆藏题名，另保留 Autumn in the Northland 作为复现品检索用名。中文作品名为图鉴译名。所有展示图均为用户提供的作品复现图，保留原文件与可见署名；同批旋纹森林另列为归属待核实对照。
judgment_note.en: Artwork information is recorded separately from stylistic judgments: dates, media and collections follow the sources linked below each image; “Post-Impressionist-like” and “decorative” are this atlas’s summaries of the visible pictorial language. Information on Autumn (1940) comes from DailyArt’s McMichael feature; no collection-database accession number was obtained in this review. The user’s image is a detail with the lower foreground cropped out. Festive Autumn uses the AGO’s current collection title; Autumn in the Northland is also retained as a search name used for reproductions. Chinese artwork titles are translations made for this atlas. All displayed images are user-provided reproductions of artworks, with the original files and visible signatures retained. The swirling forest from the same batch is listed separately as a comparison image with unverified attribution.

text.zh: 山脊、谷地和云层被概括为交叠的弧形与带状色面，重复但不等距。坡面的轮廓与笔触一起顺着地形转折，形成起伏、流动的节奏。
text.en: Ridgelines, valleys and clouds are simplified into overlapping arcs and bands of color, repeated at uneven intervals. The contours and brushwork on slopes follow the turns of the terrain together, creating an undulating, flowing rhythm.

text.zh: 金黄、橙红和赭红集中在受光坡面与叶丛；深青、蓝绿和冷蓝组织林间、背光面与远景。同一山丘上的明暗分区清楚，暖色鲜艳处仍有深色支撑。
text.en: Golden yellow, orange-red and russet concentrate on sunlit slopes and foliage; deep teal, blue-green and cool blue organize woodland interiors, shaded planes and the distance. Light and shade on each hill are clearly divided, while dark colors still support the vivid warm areas.

text.zh: 大形先用相对完整的色面组织，再以短笔、条带、点触和不规则碎色块塑造细部。方向性的笔触交代山势、云带与地面，而树叶常以分离的小亮色块点出。
text.en: Major forms are first organized as relatively continuous color areas, then details are shaped with short strokes, bands, dabs and irregular patches of broken color. Directional brushwork describes hills, cloud bands and ground, while leaves are often indicated with separate small patches of bright color.

text.zh: 白桦树干与细枝提供浅色、弯曲的竖线，深色针叶树呈紧凑剪影，暖色树冠以概括轮廓组织。这些形体在秋林样例中交错，既框景，也把视线送入谷地。
text.en: Birch trunks and fine branches provide pale, curved vertical lines; dark conifers form compact silhouettes, and warm canopies are organized with simplified contours. These forms interweave in the autumn woodland examples, both framing the view and directing the eye into the valley.

text.zh: 前景保留岩石、树干与强烈暗部，远景使用较冷、较浅的蓝绿色；坡面的斑块亮部带出日光。空间层次由遮挡、色温和明暗共同建立，局部形式则保持装饰性。
text.en: Rocks, trunks and strong shadows remain in the foreground, while cooler, lighter blue-greens occupy the distance; patches of light on the slopes suggest sunlight. Overlap, color temperature and value work together to establish spatial layers, while individual forms retain a decorative character.

text.zh: 《Autumn》（1940）偏重宽阔山势与云层；《October Gold》（1922）以白桦和密集金叶框住深色谷地；《Festive Autumn》（1921）用树木、伐木遗迹、岩石和散布光斑形成明亮的前景。三幅共享色彩与形体节奏，笔触疏密各有不同。
text.en: Autumn (1940) emphasizes broad hills and clouds; October Gold (1922) frames a dark valley with birches and dense golden foliage; Festive Autumn (1921) creates a bright foreground from trees, traces of logging, rocks and scattered patches of light. The three share rhythms of color and form, while varying in brushstroke density.

legacy_prompts.zh: 将输入照片完整改绘为 Franklin Carmichael 秋色风景所体现的绘画语言：概括而有节奏的形体、鲜明冷暖色块与方向性的短笔触。输入照片决定内容、构图和空间；附加参考仅提供风格。保留原图主体数量、人物身份与姿态、主要物件关系、地形或建筑结构、视角和画幅比例。先用交叠的大色面重建明暗，把已有山势、道路、云层、树冠或建筑体块整理为清晰、有机的轮廓，让弧线与带状色面顺着实际形体起伏。以深青、蓝绿和冷蓝组织阴影及远景，以金黄、橙红和赭红处理原场景已有的受光面与暖色对象；保留浅色天空或背景的呼吸空间，避免所有区域同样鲜艳。以短笔、条带、点触与不规则碎色表现已有叶丛、岩石、织物和地面，方向随形体变化，保持笔触疏密与清晰的大结构。植物可概括为浅色树干、深色树群和暖色叶簇；人物面部保留可辨认特征，并用与全画一致的笔触重绘。近景有明确遮挡和暗部，远景较冷、较浅，使装饰性色块仍有空间纵深。不要从参考导入山丘、白桦、树桩、倒木或新人物；不要强行改变季节、镜头或画幅。避免均匀旋纹、连续等距刻槽、满屏细节、摄影贴片、塑料光泽、文字、水印，以及仅叠加鲜艳色彩滤镜。
legacy_prompts.en: Repaint the entire input photograph using the visual language of Franklin Carmichael’s autumn landscapes: simplified rhythmic forms, distinct warm and cool color masses, and directional short brushstrokes. Let the input photograph determine content, composition and space; use additional references for style only. Preserve the original subject count, people’s identities and poses, key object relationships, terrain or architectural structure, viewpoint and aspect ratio. Reconstruct light and shade with broad overlapping color areas first, then organize existing hills, paths, clouds, canopies or building masses into clear organic contours, letting arcs and bands of color rise and fall with the actual forms. Use deep teal, blue-green and cool blue for shadows and distance, and golden yellow, orange-red and russet for the original scene’s existing sunlit planes and warm-colored objects. Retain breathing room in a pale sky or background and avoid making every area equally vivid. Render existing foliage, rocks, fabric and ground with short strokes, bands, dabs and irregular broken color, varying direction with the forms and preserving varied brushstroke density and a clear overall structure. Vegetation may be simplified into pale trunks, dark tree masses and warm leaf clusters. Retain recognizable facial features and repaint them with brushwork consistent with the whole image. Keep clear overlaps and shadows in the foreground and cooler, lighter distance, so decorative color masses still have spatial depth. Do not import hills, birches, stumps, fallen logs or new people from the references; do not force a change of season, camera view or frame. Avoid uniform swirls, continuous evenly spaced grooves, detail filling the entire image, photographic patches, plastic gloss, text, watermarks, and merely overlaying a vivid color filter.
